newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA'S PETROM STARTS AMBITIOUS REFORM PROGRAMME.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA'S PETROM STARTS AMBITIOUS REFORM PROGRAMME.

text.p: Romania has launched an ambitious programme to restructure and privatise its oil and gas sector in a bid to reverse a long decline in its production, a senior official said on Friday.

Under the project, state-run Petrom RA oil authority will launch an "aggressive" exploitation of oil and gas deposits at big depths, in joint projects with foreign firms, Secretary of state Liviu Marcu told a Crans Montana Forum in Bucharest.
Petrom's oil and gas output covers some 30 percent of Romania's energy resources.

The plan also includes investments in infrastructure, a commercial-oriented activity of Petrom to make units within its structure competitive and attractive to foreign investors, as well as steps to stop the decline in oil output.
The split of Petrom in joint stock companies, a process expected to be completed within the next three months, would lay the ground for privatisation, Marcu said.
"We are ready to sell any stake in Petrom," Marcu said, adding that the company planned to retain the so-called golden shares giving it the right to veto.
Better cooperation with foreign partners and international lenders and a more flexible management are also part of the package to be completed by year 2000.
In January, Petrom said it hoped to raise some $150 million from an Eurobond issue through Merrill Lynch . It also announced plans for a $100 million syndicated loan for investment.

Romania, a mature oil and gas producing region which began commercial production of oil in the 1860s, has seen a constant decline in its output over the past years, mainly due to frenzied exploitation of oil and gas reserves and use of poor equipment under the former communist regime, ousted in 1989.
Crude production was around 6.7 million tonnes last year, compared to a peak output of 14.7 million in 1986. Marcu said Petrom hoped to maintain the 1997 oil and gas output on last year's level.
A gas output of 17.1 billion cubic metres is expected this year, when imports are seen at 7.0 billion cubic metres.
Romania issued legislation to protect foreign investment, a new petroleum law putting local and foreign firms on equal footing and a bill allowing foreigners to buy land.

Analysts say Romania holds the best oil and gas exploration prospects in central Europe. The potential for new commercial oil finds is there but unexploited fields are expected to be deep and trapped in complex geological structures, they say.
The country needs capital and modern technology to discover new oil deposits or revitalize old ones. Local oil companies drill only at depths of 4,000 metres.
The National Agency for Mineral Resources is expected to announce soon the winners in a licensing round for 15 prospective onshore and offshore oil blocks.
